From 2933bf3528007f834fb7f5eab033f9c5b0683f91 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Qiang Yu <yuq825@gmail.com>
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2020 14:27:55 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] arm64: dts: allwinner: h5: remove Mali GPU PMU module

H5's Mali GPU PMU is not present or working corretly although
H5 datasheet record its interrupt vector.

Adding this module will miss lead lima driver try to shutdown
it and get waiting timeout. This problem is not exposed before
lima runtime PM support is added.

Fixes: bb39ed07e55b ("arm64: dts: allwinner: h5: Add device node for Mali-450 GPU")
Signed-off-by: Qiang Yu <yuq825@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Maxime Ripard <maxime@cerno.tech>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20200822062755.534761-1-yuq825@gmail.com

diff --git a/arch/arm64/boot/dts/allwinner/sun50i-h5.dtsi b/arch/arm64/boot/dts/allwinner/sun50i-h5.dtsi
index 6735e316a39c..6c6053a18413 100644
--- a/arch/arm64/boot/dts/allwinner/sun50i-h5.dtsi
+++ b/arch/arm64/boot/dts/allwinner/sun50i-h5.dtsi
@@ -139,8 +139,7 @@ mali: gpu@1e80000 {
 				     <GIC_SPI 104 IRQ_TYPE_LEVEL_HIGH>,
 				     <GIC_SPI 105 IRQ_TYPE_LEVEL_HIGH>,
 				     <GIC_SPI 106 IRQ_TYPE_LEVEL_HIGH>,
-				     <GIC_SPI 107 IRQ_TYPE_LEVEL_HIGH>,
-				     <GIC_SPI 98 IRQ_TYPE_LEVEL_HIGH>;
+				     <GIC_SPI 107 IRQ_TYPE_LEVEL_HIGH>;
 			interrupt-names = "gp",
 					  "gpmmu",
 					  "pp",
@@ -151,8 +150,7 @@ mali: gpu@1e80000 {
 					  "pp2",
 					  "ppmmu2",
 					  "pp3",
-					  "ppmmu3",
-					  "pmu";
+					  "ppmmu3";
 			clocks = <&ccu CLK_BUS_GPU>, <&ccu CLK_GPU>;
 			clock-names = "bus", "core";
 			resets = <&ccu RST_BUS_GPU>;
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `arch/arm64/boot/dts/allwinner/sun50i-h5.dtsi`**
   - Removed the entry for the Mali GPU PMU module from the device tree source (DTS) file. Specifically:
     - The line defining the PMU interrupt (`<GIC_SPI 98 IRQ_TYPE_LEVEL_HIGH>;`) was deleted.
     - The entry for the PMU in the `interrupt-names` list was also removed.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The modifications made in the DTS file are aimed at correcting a misconfiguration related to the Mali GPU PMU module. The removal of the PMU entry is necessary because the Mali GPU PMU is either absent or not functioning correctly on the H5 platform. This change prevents the lima driver from attempting to manage a non-existent PMU, which was causing timeouts during shutdown operations. The fix addresses an issue that became apparent after the addition of runtime power management support for the lima driver, as indicated by the reference to a previous commit that introduced the Mali GPU device node.

Here is the commit message:
arm64: dts: allwinner: h5: remove Mali GPU PMU module

H5's Mali GPU PMU is not present or working corretly although
H5 datasheet record its interrupt vector.

Adding this module will miss lead lima driver try to shutdown
it and get waiting timeout. This problem is not exposed before
lima runtime PM support is added.

Fixes: bb39ed07e55b ("arm64: dts: allwinner: h5: Add device node for Mali-450 GPU")
Signed-off-by: Qiang Yu <yuq825@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Maxime Ripard <maxime@cerno.tech>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20200822062755.534761-1-yuq825@gmail.com

Here is the root cause:
The root cause of the bug is the incorrect inclusion of the Mali GPU PMU module in the device tree source (DTS) for the Allwinner H5 platform. Although the H5 datasheet records an interrupt vector for the PMU, the module is either not present or not functioning correctly. This misconfiguration leads the lima driver to attempt to manage the PMU during shutdown, resulting in a waiting timeout when the driver cannot communicate with a non-existent or non-functional PMU.

Here is the patch:
 				     <GIC_SPI 105 IRQ_TYPE_LEVEL_HIGH>,
 				     <GIC_SPI 106 IRQ_TYPE_LEVEL_HIGH>,
-				     <GIC_SPI 107 IRQ_TYPE_LEVEL_HIGH>,
-				     <GIC_SPI 98 IRQ_TYPE_LEVEL_HIGH>;
+				     <GIC_SPI 107 IRQ_TYPE_LEVEL_HIGH>;
 			interrupt-names = "gp",
 					  "gpmmu",
 					  "ppmmu2",
 					  "pp3",
-					  "ppmmu3",
-					  "pmu";
+					  "ppmmu3";
 			clocks = <&ccu CLK_BUS_GPU>, <&ccu CLK_GPU>;
 			clock-names = "bus", "core";

Reason:
The inclusion of the Mali GPU PMU module in the device tree source (DTS) for the Allwinner H5 platform is incorrect because the PMU is either not present or not functioning correctly. This misconfiguration causes the lima driver to attempt to manage the PMU during shutdown, leading to a waiting timeout when it cannot communicate with the non-existent or non-functional PMU.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```dts
+				     <GIC_SPI 107 IRQ_TYPE_LEVEL_HIGH>;
+					  "pmu";
```
Reason:
By removing the references to the non-existent PMU module in the device tree, the patch prevents the lima driver from attempting to manage the PMU during shutdown. This change eliminates the waiting timeout issue, as the driver will no longer look for a PMU that is not present or functioning.
